messages.author: 5c834f66d44ea056
messages.subject: INLA crashing while Spatial Analysis
parts:
Hello INLA experts,

I have a data set that has around 15500 observations and I am running a spatial model as following:

fit.pred_2<-inla(owtob ~ agec + male+MedianIncome+f(struct, model="bym",graph = W),
                 family="binomial",
                 data=merged_new, control.fixed = list(expand.factor.strategy='inla'),
                 control.predictor = list(link=1),verbose=TRUE
)

The above model crashed after 3-4 hours of running giving a message  Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed(). The same model worked with around 10000 observations.
Then reading some previous similar issues  I changed my  model  and used the following model with eb,ccd and grip as  the integration strategies and keeping the strategy as default (I think simplified.laplace)for 155000 observations 

fit.pred_2<-inla(owtob ~ agec + male+MedianIncome+f(struct, model="bym2",graph = W),
                 family="binomial",
                 data=merged_new, control.fixed = list(expand.factor.strategy='inla'),
                 control.predictor = list(link=1),verbose=TRUE, control.inla = list(int.strategy = "ccd/grid/eb")
)

With eb and ccd it worked fine but with grid again it crashed after 3-4 hours . Is it because of memory issues or  should I change some other parameters?

I would really appreciate if some help is available to understand the difference among these integration strategies as it working with couple and not working with some of them.
I have attached the verbose files for both models (the model 1 and the model with "grid" as the integration strategy).

Thanks!

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA crashing while Spatial Analysis
parts:
it seems like you have issues with memory, use the default option for
int.strategy (ie, do not change it), but change

control.inla=list(strategy="adaptive")

by reducing number of threads (argument num.threads=2, f.ex), you will
use less memory. or buy more...


for the difference, you can consult one of the open-books, like the one
by Virgilio or the SPDE book, for explanation; see r-inla.org/books

H

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA crashing while Spatial Analysis
parts:
'grid' is only applicable for small number of hyperpar, and default its
in use for dim=1 and 2, only.

there is the function

inla.hyperpar()

which you can rerun afterwards, to do a finer analysis; see
?inla.hyperpar
